verbalization: Decarine is implicated in the pathway leading to Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 7 through multiple indirect routes. The drug targets several entities, including Ribosomal protein S6 kinase 2 and Liver X receptor (LXR alpha and LXR beta), which in turn target 2'-Hydroxymatteucinol. This 2'-Hydroxymatteucinol further targets the Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 7, establishing a chain of interactions. Additionally, Decarine is also linked to D-aspartate oxidase, which indirectly leads to the same target. The evidence suggests that Decarine may influence the activity of this enzyme through a series of intermediate targets, potentially modulating its function in cellular processes. The integration of these pathways highlights the drug's potential to affect the enzyme through multiple mechanisms, emphasizing the role of 2'-Hydroxymatteucinol as a central mediator in the relationship between Decarine and the Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 7.
